insights.title: Preserve the core 7 Series promise: serene, smooth, spacious, prestigious driving luxury
insights.description: Across the selected markets, the strongest customer value is still the classic 7 Series combination of quietness, ride comfort, space, prestige/equipment and effortless driving. The successor should protect these limousine fundamentals before adding more novelty.
vfc_topics: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology

score 98.0, mean 9.82/10
score 97.5, mean 9.78/10
score 94.6, mean 9.52/10
score 86.7, mean 6.20/7, top-2 75%, bottom-3 1%
it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious
fantastic car to drive and super comfortable

conflicting_signals: US verbatims include strong praise for driving comfort and quietness, but also some severe wind/cabin-noise complaints.
CN and EU study scores are extremely strong on quietness/ride, while US study scores are positive but lower on several interaction/value attributes.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims; CN conclusions rely on study and sales data only.
Only 19 EU feedback verbatims; EU comfort/quietness conclusion is primarily study-based.

insights.title: Digital luxury is not yet effortless enough; software reliability and learnability are flagship hygiene
insights.description: US customers repeatedly describe iDrive, infotainment, navigation, app and screen behavior as glitchy or complicated. For a flagship, customers expect advanced technology to feel calmer, more self-explanatory and more reliable, not to require reboots, dealer trips or extensive learning.

evidence.detail: there are software glitches in idrive 8
the display suddenly went blank and nothing on the screen would operate

score 56.0, mean 4.36/7, top-2 25%, bottom-3 26%
score 59.6, mean 4.57/7, top-2 32%, bottom-3 21%

evidence.ref: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps
evidence.detail: score 78.9, mean 8.10/10
score 86.9, mean 8.82/10

conflicting_signals: The pain is strongest in US verbatims and US study attributes; CN and EU study scores for infotainment/navigation are materially better.
Some customers praise the overall technology while still criticizing specific software reliability or complexity.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims to explain whether study satisfaction hides specific software frustrations.
EU feedback sample is too small to judge whether EU owners experience the same software pain as US owners.

insights.title: Customers want personal settings, shortcuts and key controls to persist without menu-diving
insights.description: A recurring US need is not just simpler HMI, but control over the car’s behavior: preferred drive mode, start-stop, massage, climate, ambient light and widgets should be quick to access and remember the driver’s preferences. At this price point, repeated setup every drive feels out of place.

evidence.detail: he has to go into the app and switch it off every time he drives
a dedicated physical button that can switch off the Automatic Engine Start-Stop function
start up directly in his preferred mode
a dedicated physical button to quickly switch the massaging seats on or off
having no knobs or buttons seems unncessary. i would really like at least a knob for the aircon
two independent ambient lighting brightness controls

evidence.ref: STUDY:US:Placement/ ease of reading and using controls
evidence.detail: score 58.4, mean 4.51/7, top-2 30%, bottom-3 24%
all the voice and touch controls and the whole layout are fantastic

conflicting_signals: Some owners enjoy the digital/voice/touch control concept, while others want physical shortcuts and persistent defaults for the same functions.
The need is most visible in US feedback; it is not validated by CN or EU verbatims.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims and very limited EU verbatims on control preferences.
No option-penetration data to show how many owners have the affected features.

insights.title: BEV and PHEV customers need ICE-like confidence in range, charging and trip planning
insights.description: US i7/750e feedback shows that customers love the EV driving experience but can lose confidence when real-world range, winter range, route planning and public-charger availability do not match expectations. For the successor launch horizon, range and charging confidence should feel as premium as the vehicle itself.

evidence.detail: misled me about the range and i have already been stranded
below 10 degrees it will not even reach 150 miles on a full charge
the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available
i usually wait well over half an hour just in line, and then about another 30 minutes to actually charge
about 2/3 of the chargers are either not working or already in use
having at least 100 miles available would be extremely helpful
score 66.5, mean 4.99/7, top-2 32%, bottom-3 7%
the real world range is quite good
For a 3-5 year successor, premium BEV/PHEV customers are expected to compare charging predictability with ICE refueling convenience.

conflicting_signals: Some US i7 owners report good real-world range, while others report severe winter range loss and range anxiety.
The strongest charging pain comes from BEV feedback; PHEV feedback focuses more on desire for longer electric-only range.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims; CN EV expectations are not directly captured in the provided feedback.
No EU BEV/PHEV verbatim base large enough to validate charging pain.
Sales are not split by powertrain, so the scale of BEV/PHEV impact by market is unknown.

insights.title: Rear-seat luxury is a major delighter, but theater, connectivity and rear comfort must not compromise each other
insights.description: Rear comfort and the theatrical cabin experience are core to the 7 Series’ flagship role. US feedback shows delight in theater mode and rear-seat amenities, but also friction when the screen blocks visibility, forces front-seat movement, depends on unreliable eSIM/connectivity, or when rear massage/TV content is unclear or missing.

conflicting_signals: US study scores for second-row comfort/room are very strong, yet US verbatims expose feature-integration pain around theater mode and eSIM.
EU rear roominess is very strong in the study, while CN rear roominess is comparatively lower within the CN attribute set.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims, despite rear-seat experience being particularly important to validate for China.
EU feedback base is too small to understand rear entertainment/connectivity pain.

insights.title: Cocoon-like acoustic and build quality must be consistent, not just good on average
insights.description: Quietness is a flagship strength in studies, but a subset of US owners report wind noise, road noise, mirror noise, trim issues and creaks that feel unacceptable in a six-figure BMW. The customer need is consistency: every car should deliver the promised cocoon effect.

evidence.ref: STUDY:US:Freedom from wind and road noise
evidence.detail: score 80.5, mean 5.83/7, top-2 64%, bottom-3 6%
score 97.5, mean 9.78/10

conflicting_signals: Study data says quietness is a major strength in all three markets; US verbatims show that when acoustic defects occur, they strongly damage perceived build quality.
BEV feedback can be exceptionally positive on quietness, while some ICE feedback calls out wind/cabin noise.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims to identify whether quietness issues occur in China.
EU feedback sample is too small to verify whether the very high EU quietness score masks specific noise complaints.

insights.title: Climate comfort needs to be more powerful, more predictable and easier to control
insights.description: US customers flag both HVAC performance and HVAC interaction: slow cooling, weak airflow, delayed warmth, settings that do not stay synced, and desire for rules or a simple knob. There is also an emerging wellbeing use case for keeping the cabin comfortable for pets or passengers when the driver steps away.

No seasonal/climate-zone split is provided, so climate performance pain may be region- or weather-dependent.

insights.title: Automatic doors are a wow feature only if they are fast, safe and easier than manual doors
insights.description: US customers like the idea of power doors, but the current experience can feel slow, unfinished, hard to reach, resistant when operated manually, or unsafe if buttons are accidentally triggered in gear. The need is for theatrical convenience that also feels trustworthy in everyday use.

evidence.detail: Automatic Doors are cool, but also commented that they are very slow

score 75.8, mean 5.55/7, top-2 52%, bottom-3 3%

conflicting_signals: Automatic doors are both a delighter and a pain point: customers praise the idea, but criticize speed, ergonomics and perceived safety.
US study feedback on exterior door handles is broadly positive, while verbatims highlight specific automatic-door scenarios.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims and no EU verbatims on automatic doors in the provided sample.
No data on whether complaints are concentrated in a software version, production period or usage scenario.

insights.title: Driver assistance is valued, but customers expect smoother, clearer and more capable automation
insights.description: Highway assistance reduces stress for some owners, yet US feedback shows trust issues around harsh braking, confusing mode differences, limited operating domains and comparisons with Tesla-like autonomy. Over the successor horizon, customers are likely to expect driver assistance to feel more human, transparent and destination-capable.

conflicting_signals: Some US owners are impressed by Driver Assist Plus, while others distrust braking behavior or find mode boundaries confusing.

data_gaps: No CN verbatims on autonomy/ADAS expectations.

The data does not separate vehicles by exact driver-assistance option content or software level.

insights.title: Flagship pricing and packaging must feel generous, transparent and complete
insights.description: Value-for-money is a weak point especially in EU and US study results. Customers paying six-figure prices react strongly when expected comfort features are extra, excluded from packages, subscription-dependent, unclear at order time, or not working after payment.

conflicting_signals: CN study data is much more positive on value and equipment than EU/US data.

EU verbatim base is very small, though the EU study value score is low.

insights.title: Design should stay distinctive but become less polarizing and more timelessly BMW
insights.description: Study data indicates exterior and interior styling are generally valued, but US verbatims show some customers perceive the exterior as too bulky/aggressive, the light signature as losing BMW heritage, and some interior/ambient elements as too showy or cheap. The opportunity is to keep flagship presence while offering more timeless, configurable expressions of luxury.

evidence.detail: score 86.5, mean 8.79/10
score 82.0, mean 8.38/10
score 76.0, mean 5.56/7, top-2 53%, bottom-3 2%

conflicting_signals: Styling scores are positive in all three markets, especially CN, while US verbatims show polarization around specific cues.
Interior crystal controls are praised by one owner and rejected by others, suggesting preference diversity rather than a single winning treatment.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims to understand which design cues drive the high CN styling score.
No EU design verbatims in the provided sample; EU interpretation is study-only.

insights.title: Size and practicality need balance: flagship presence should not make daily use harder
insights.description: Some US owners experience the G70 as too wide, long or bulky for garages and daily maneuvering, while others praise its roominess. CN study scores also point to roominess/loading/luggage as relative watchouts. The next generation needs to retain spaciousness and presence while reducing perceived bulk and improving practical storage/use cases.

score 71.8, mean 7.46/10
score 74.0, mean 7.66/10

score 96.5, mean 9.69/10
score 93.4, mean 9.41/10

conflicting_signals: US feedback is split between too bulky/cramped in some zones and very roomy overall.
EU roominess study scores are very high, while CN luggage/loading/rear roominess scores are comparatively weaker.
The size pain may depend heavily on local parking/garage context, which is not captured in the data.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims to explain the relatively lower CN loading/luggage/roominess scores.
EU feedback sample is too small to assess real-world parking or garage pain.
No dimensional/garage-context data is provided.

insight_caveats: No customer feedback verbatims are provided for China; CN conclusions rely on customer-study and sales data in this package.
Only 19 feedback verbatims are provided for Europe, so EU verbatim-based conclusions are weak and study-led.
189 verbatims from outside CN/EU/US are excluded from market-specific interpretation.
US verbatims dominate the feedback sample; US pain points should be validated before being treated as universal.
Customer-study scales differ by region, especially US 7-point derived scores versus CN/EU 10-point derived scores, so cross-market comparisons should be directional.
Sales data is total 7 Series volume by market and is not split by powertrain, option package or body/use case.
